svg.aria-label: Four causal pathways · membrane orientation and cell response
svg.text: How receptor mechanisms differ
Four causal pathways · membrane orientation and cell response
1. Ligand-gated ion channel
Outside: acetylcholine binds its membrane receptor
Channel opens → net inward cation movement
Inside: membrane depolarization may reach threshold
2. G protein-coupled receptor
Outside: epinephrine binds the membrane GPCR
Inside: Gs activates adenylyl cyclase → cAMP
cAMP activates PKA → protein phosphorylation
3. Receptor tyrosine kinase
Outside: insulin binds its plasma-membrane receptor
Inside: tyrosine phosphorylation → signalling cascade
GLUT4 vesicles fuse → facilitated glucose uptake
4. Intracellular steroid receptor
Lipid-soluble steroid enters the target cell
Intracellular receptor activates and binds regulatory DNA
Changed transcription → altered protein production
The ligand, receptor location and downstream response all matter.
Simplified mechanisms, not to molecular scale. Signal timing varies.
